name: Duchy of Parma and Piacenza
alt: Duchy of Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla

predecessors.name: First French Empire
predecessors.text: 'In 1814, the duchies were given to Napoleon's Habsburg wife, Marie-Louise'

successors.name: United Provinces of Central Italy
successors.text: 'In December 1859, the Duchy of Parma and Piacenza was combined with the Grand Duchy of Tuscany and the Duchy of Modena to form the United Provinces of Central Italy'

ledger.x: 11 April 1814: the duchies of Parma and Piacenza pass to Marie Louise.
17 December 1847: Parma cedes Guastalla to Modena.
17 December 1847: Parma receives the Tuscan enclaves of Lunigiana.
17 December 1847: Marie Louise dies and the duchy passes from the Habsburg duchess to the Bourbon-Parma.
1848: Parma leaves its duke and votes for union with Sardinia.
August 1848: Parma returns to its duke after the armistice of Salasco.
8 December 1859: Parma is ceded to the United Provinces of Central Italy.

wars.name: Revolution of 1848 in Parma
wars.outcome: The Bourbon-Parma regime was 'temporarily' driven out by 'an uprising in 1848'; the dukes returned and no land changed hands on this page.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: 'driven out by a revolution following the French and Sardinian victory' in 1859; Parma joined the United Provinces of Central Italy on 8 December 1859 and Sardinia in March 1860.

certainty.note: Borders with Modena, Tuscany and Sardinia were fixed by the Final Act and the 1844 Treaty of Florence; Cliopatria's outline is coarse (about one H3 cell, 250 km2, of error).
